title: The Diamond PAU runs at a hundredth of the monolithic controller's limits, marking it as a live pilot beside the production system
content:
Comparing A.6.1.1.2.2.6.1.2.1.1.3.1.1 (monolithic ALM, Ethereum Mainnet) with A.6.1.1.2.2.6.1.2.1.1.3.2 (Diamond PAU, Ethereum Mainnet) shows a deliberate two-order-of-magnitude gap. The monolith's USDS mint limit is 500,000,000 with a matching daily slope; the Diamond PAU's is 5,000,000. The same ratio holds for the USDS-for-USDC PSM swap limit.

Read alongside the separate capitalization in A.6.1.1.2.2.6.1.2.1.1.1.1.1.1 — ALLOCATOR-BLOOM-A funds the monolith, ALLOCATOR-GROVE-A funds the Diamond PAU — the picture is a **strangler-fig migration**. The new architecture is deployed in production against real capital, with its own vault and its own controller, but sized so that a failure is survivable while the old system continues carrying the book.

Two details make the Diamond PAU look like the intended successor rather than a permanent niche. It has a **symmetric** limit set — both USDS mint and USDS burn are specified, and both PSM directions (USDS→USDC and USDC→USDS) are populated — whereas the monolith's burn limit and several of its domain limits are still marked "will be specified in a future iteration." And its architecture is the one the Sky Core Atlas shares across Agents.

The practical reading for anyone assessing Grove's risk surface is that there are currently **two independent execution paths** into the same protocols, with different code, different vaults, different rate limits and different role wiring. Any statement about Grove's controls has to specify which path it describes.
description: Its controller-wide USDS mint, burn and PSM swap allowances are two orders of magnitude below the monolith's, and it is capitalized from a separate Allocator Vault.
